label: Late-episode clock at D2 (trial >= ~83 after a1, >= ~94 after a2)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1 or GO), and only in the last ~20 trials of the 100-trial episode: none before trial 70, 7% of D2 steps at trials 80-89, 24% at 90-99. It turns on earlier and fires more when this trial chose a1 (82% of mass is a1 at D2): on a1 trials it starts around trial 83, on a2 trials only around trial 94. Magnitude rises toward the end of the episode, and the top windows fall at the final trials. Reached state, transition (common or rare), reward history, good state and stay/switch add little beyond the action; state works worse than action. Its activity matches low value-head output (85% of mass is in the lowest value bin), which fits the model expecting less reward as the episode runs out. Every variable used (phase, the episode-trial clock, and this trial choice shown as in_action at D2) is observed at D2. Dev F1 0.86 vs 0.72 for phase plus clock alone.

issues: Every factual claim I checked holds. The feature fires only at D2 (0 active steps at D1 and at GO). It never fires before trial 70; it is active on 386 steps at trials 70-79 (rate 0.003), 7.2% at 80-89 and 24.4% at 90-99. 81.7% of activation mass is on a1 trials. 85% of mass is in the lowest value bin. The reached-state version of the predicate does worse (test F1 0.771 vs 0.847 for the action version). Clock alone, (phase==D2)&(ep_trial>=88), gets test F1 0.732. Value<5.22 alone gets test F1 0.707.

I reproduced the scores. Dev: P 0.812, R 0.905, F1 0.856. Test: P 0.795, R 0.905, F1 0.847, mass recall 0.970. Missed activations hold only 3.0% of mass and are small, scattered activations near the a1/a2 onset boundaries.

The false positives are graded rather than a separate class. The onset is soft, not a sharp cut: precision is 0.60 at trials 83-89 inside the predicate and 0.89 at trials 95 and later. There is also secondary modulation inside the predicate. Precision is 0.85 for a1->S1 vs 0.73 for a1->S2, 0.91 for a2->S1 vs 0.68 for a2->S2, 0.87 for prev_reward==0 vs 0.75 for prev_reward==1, and 0.67 when good==2 vs 0.83 when good==1. So reaching S1 and having no reward on the previous trial shift the onset earlier, on top of the action. This contradicts the explanation's claim that the reached state and reward history 'add little', but only mildly.

An observed-only additive threshold that captures this, (phase==D2)&(ep_trial >= 96 - 7*(action==1) - 4*(state==1) - 3*(prev_reward==0)), reaches test F1 0.870 (dev 0.872), a gain of about 0.02. Adding the hidden good state gives test F1 0.880. These are refinements of the same late-episode-clock-at-D2 story, not a counterexample class, so I uphold the label.
